chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from a freedman of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from the people of al-Madinah, who said:
I saw Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) ascend al-Marwah, then threw himself onto the stone that is at its highest point, within easy reach, and faced the Ka'bah.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى: Abu al-Hasan Musa, referring to Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحَجَر: The stone, specifically referring to the marker or stone at the top of Marwah
key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cubic building at the Grand Mosque in Mecca, the focal point of prayer
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwah, the sacred hill in Mecca between which pilgrims walk during Sa'i

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kazim do on al-Marwah during his pilgrimage?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the devotional practice of Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) on al-Marwah, illustrating the deep spiritual reverence associated with the Sa'i ritual. By casting himself upon the highest stone while facing the Ka'bah, he emphasized the physical and spiritual connection between the two sacred boundaries, reinforcing the significance of al-Marwah as a symbol of God's boundaries (Sa'd Allah). This act serves as a practical model for pilgrims, linking the historical ritual of Hajar to the eternal presence of the Imams.
